related_questions.question: What does Cryptosporidium mean?
related_questions.snippet: Cryptosporidiosis is a disease that causes watery diarrhea. It is caused by a microscopic germ (parasite) called Cryptosporidium. This parasite can live in water, food, soil, or on surfaces that have been contaminated with infected poop. Cryptosporidium can be found in the United States and throughout the world.
related_questions.title: About Crypto Infections | Cryptosporidium ("Crypto") - CDC

text_blocks.snippet: Cryptosporidiosis, also known as "Crypto," is caused by the parasite Cryptosporidium. This parasite is found in the feces of infected humans and animals and can contaminate various sources like water, food, soil, and surfaces. Infection occurs when someone swallows the parasite, often through contaminated water or by touching a contaminated surface and then their mouth, nose, or eyes.

list.title: The Parasite:
list.snippet: Cryptosporidium is a microscopic parasite that lives in the intestines of infected individuals and animals.

list.title: Transmission:
list.snippet: Cryptosporidium is primarily spread through the fecal-oral route, meaning it's ingested after being passed in the feces of an infected person or animal.

list.title: Contaminated Sources:
list.snippet: The parasite can contaminate various sources, including:
Water: Recreational water sources like swimming pools, lakes, and public water supplies.
Food: Raw fruits and vegetables that haven't been washed or peeled, unpasteurized milk, and cider.
Surfaces: Anything contaminated with infected feces, such as playground equipment or bathroom surfaces.

list.title: Risk Factors:
list.snippet: Certain groups are more susceptible to infection, including:
Young children: Especially those in childcare centers.
People with weakened immune systems: Those with HIV/AIDS, transplant recipients, or those taking immunosuppressant medications.
People who work with animals: Especially those who work with cattle, sheep, or other farm animals.
Travelers to areas with poor sanitation: .
Individuals who swallow contaminated water: Swimmers, backpackers, and hikers who drink unfiltered water.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Cryptosporidiosis can cause watery diarrhea, stomach cramps, fever, nausea, and weight loss. Symptoms usually appear within 2-10 days of infection and can last for a few weeks.

list.title: Prevention:
list.snippet: Good hygiene practices, such as thorough handwashing and food preparation, can help prevent the spread of Cryptosporidium. Proper water treatment and filtration are also crucial.

related_questions.question: Is Cryptosporidium a virus or bacteria?

text_blocks.snippet: Cryptosporidium is a parasite, specifically a protozoan, not a bacterium or a virus. It causes the diarrheal disease cryptosporidiosis. This parasite is protected by an outer shell, allowing it to survive outside the body for extended periods and making it chlorine-resistant.
snippet_highlighted_words: Cryptosporidium is a parasite, specifically a protozoan, not a bacterium or a virus

list.title: Protozoan:
list.snippet: Cryptosporidium belongs to the group of single-celled eukaryotic organisms called protozoa.

list.title: Not Bacteria or Virus:
list.snippet: Unlike bacteria (which are prokaryotic, single-celled organisms) and viruses (which are not even considered living cells), Cryptosporidium is a more complex organism with a defined nucleus and other cellular structures.

list.title: Transmission:
list.snippet: Cryptosporidium is typically spread through contaminated water or food, or through contact with infected feces.

list.title: Disease:
list.snippet: The parasite causes cryptosporidiosis, a diarrheal illness that can be mild to severe, especially in individuals with weakened immune systems.
